title: [i18n] The list sort panel's relational hint recommends a formula field, which the server refuses to sort by (400)
body:
Found while implementing #4243 (sort field fallback). Recorded, **not claimed** — different site, different fix from #4243's.

## The contradiction

`list.sortRelationalHint` is the hint the list view's Sort panel renders when it withholds relation-typed fields. Its last sentence names the remedy, in all ten locale packs (`packages/i18n/src/locales/*.ts`):

> Columns that link to another record are not listed: they can only be sorted by the stored ID, not by the name shown in the cell. **To sort by that name, add a formula field holding it.**

A `formula` field is exactly what the server refuses to order by. objectstack `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` keeps `UNMATERIALIZED_SORT_TYPES = new Set(['formula'])`, and since objectstack#6994 a sort naming one is a hard `400 INVALID_SORT` (before that it degraded silently — `200`, every row present, `asc` and `desc` byte-identical). The server's own hint for the same situation says the opposite in as many words:

> Denormalise the value onto the object (a stored field, written when the source changes) and sort by that. **Not a formula field: it is virtual**, no driver materialises a column for one, and ORDER BY on it is silently dropped.

So a user who reads our hint, follows it, and adds a formula field to sort by lands on the one type the platform will not sort. The two doors give opposite advice for the same problem.

## Why it is visible now rather than latent

Two changes moved it into view:

- objectstack#6994 turned the silent drop into a loud refusal, which is what makes the advice actively wrong rather than merely useless.
- #4243's fix widens the sort picker's base set and withholds `formula` from it. A user following the hint now adds a field that does not appear in the picker at all.

The hint predates both; nothing about it changed. It has simply been overtaken.

## Suggested fix

Re-word the remedy sentence in all ten packs to name a **stored, denormalised field** rather than a formula field — ideally in the server's vocabulary, since objectstack#6924 and objectstack#6994 deliberately use one wording across the refusal doors so an author refused twice is not sent two different ways. Note the `en` value changing means `check:i18n-drift` will require all nine other packs to follow in the same PR.

## Not this issue

- #3950 — `ObjectGrid` still offers a clickable sort header on formula columns. Same underlying server fact, different surface (the grid's `sortable` flag, not the sort panel's hint text) and a different fix.
- #4243 — the sort picker's field set and the reset-to-default affordance. That PR withholds formula fields from the picker; it deliberately does not touch this string.
